findings.title: Reflection populator recurses infinitely on recursive types
findings.message: The `populated` helper recurses through pointers and slices without tracking types it has already visited. If `Graph` ever gains a self-referential field (for example a pointer or slice back to the same struct type), the test will overflow the stack. It would not fail with a clear message.
findings.suggestion: Track the types currently being built (for example a `map[reflect.Type]bool`). Call `t.Fatalf` with an explicit message when a recursive type is encountered, rather than recursing indefinitely.

findings.title: Duplicate admission check before retain
findings.message: `retainSweepJobLocked` now runs the admission check itself, so the explicit `requireSweepSlotLocked` calls before it are redundant. There are two such callers. In `publishSweepImportLocked` the check runs twice back-to-back. In `startDCSweepLocked` it runs before `sweepSerial` is incremented. If the two checks ever diverge, the result is confusing ordering and serial or ID gaps.
findings.suggestion: Pick one place for the admission check. Either drop the early `requireSweepSlotLocked` calls in the callers, or keep only the early fail-fast in `startDCSweepLocked` and document why it is needed. Keeping it there avoids building metadata and a context for a job that will be refused.
